messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: kv-cache growth (us-east-1 / inference-runtime) - metric kv_items spiked to ~12,100,000 (baseline ~1.2M). Auto-throttle engaged. Potentially related to recent batching/tokenizer rollout. Paging oncall Ashley. Link: https://grafana.redwood/example/kv-spike
Ashley (oncall): Ack. I'm looking at the dashboards now. Observing large memory foot usage on cache nodes + continuous batching queue depth increasing.
Priya (pager): Hit this from the pager - some customer traces show 5-12s tail latencies then 502s. Two high-QPS customers (cust-a, cust-b) affected.
Miguel (serving): Adding context: we rolled out batching-v2 + tokenizer-normalize change 17m ago to canary. Hypothesis: tokenizer normalization changed prompt hashing -> cache misses -> prefix cache bloat + regen storm + heavier KV writes -> perf cliff.
Dan (sre): Agree on hypothesis. I'm seeing repeated prefix write collisions in logs: `prefix_key_collide` with increasing retry loops. CPU on cache nodes saturated by GC. Logs:```
[2026-03-15T08:12:04Z] WARN prefix_key_collide key=7f3b... attempts=8
[2026-03-15T08:12:09Z] ERROR kv_write_timeout key=7f3b...
```
Ashley (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle incoming batching (reduce max_batch_size and max_batch_tokens), 2) disable prefix cache for canary/affected clusters, 3) pause tokenizer-normalize rollout. Miguel/Dan, can you 2/3? I'll coordinate CS comms.
Miguel (serving): On it. Rolling batch-config hotfix to inference-runtime canary group now. Patch: `batching.max_batch_size=8` (was 64), `batching.max_batch_tokens=2000` (was 8000), `batching.prefetch=false`. Applying via control-plane API:```bash
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/svc/inference-runtime/patch -d '{"batching":{"max_batch_size":8,"max_batch_tokens":2000}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```
Miguel (serving): Also toggled feature flag: `prefix_cache.enabled=false` for canaries. Command in console: flipped flag and confirmed via `GET /flags?service=inference-runtime`.
Priya (pager): Executed `curl` and saw config apply succeed. Observing queue depth dropping within 60s. Will watch for regressions.
Leah (Customer Success): FYI - notified cust-a and cust-b with temporary mitigation note. Asking for ETA to restore normal perf. Customers appreciate the quick update.
Dan (sre): Quick reproduction snippet that shows tokenizer drift impact on hash:```python
# before: tokenizer.normalize = false -> hashA
# after: tokenizer.normalize = true -> hashB
promptA = "Hello, world!"
seqA = old_tokenize(promptA)  # [101, 102, ...]
seqB = new_tokenize(promptA)  # [1009, 101, ...]  # different normalization -> different key
keyA = sha256(bytes(seqA))
keyB = sha256(bytes(seqB))
# keyA != keyB -> cache duplication/regeneration
```
Ashley (oncall): Good catch. Action: roll back tokenizer-normalize flag on canary and stop further rollout. @Miguel do we have a pin to revert?
Miguel (serving): Yes - reverting canary to tokenizer-normalize=false. Revert command executed and verified. Also triggering graceful restart of affected cache pods to free GC pressure: `kubectl rollout restart sts/kv-cache -n prod-us-east-1`.
Priya (pager): Metrics update: kv_items back down from 12.1M -> 1.6M over 7m after config & flag changes. P99 latency for inference-runtime decreased from 3.8s -> 650ms. Error rate still elevated (502s) but trending down.
Dan (sre): Note: some stale writeback backlog exists; we'll let caches drain rather than force mass eviction. Also increased retention on write-retry for a short window to avoid additional thrash.
Leah (Customer Success): Shared interim status with customers: mitigation applied, latency improving, engineering monitoring. Asking for impact quant: cust-a saw ~6% error rate for last 20m, cust-b ~3%. Both accepted the temporary note.
Ashley (oncall): Incident severity: Sev2. Root cause candidate: tokenizer normalization change causing prompt hash divergence and prefix cache inflation under continuous batching workload; combo with batching-v2 config allowed larger prefix fanout -> KV cache blowup.
Miguel (serving): Post-mitigation checklist: 1) block tokenizer-normalize rollout until postmortem, 2) add rolling 'prompt-to-key' sampler to catch hash distribution changes in canary, 3) baseline batch-config stress tests before rollout.
Priya (pager): Handoff: I'm handing oncall to Miguel at 08:00 UTC. Miguel, you own next 2hr watch and the customer sync.
Miguel (serving): Ack handoff. I'll monitor and open a follow-up playbook PR with explicit limiter defaults for batching.
Ashley (oncall): Thanks team. We'll schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 PT. Owners: Miguel (runtime), Dan (infra), Priya (ops), Leah (customer impact). Add timeline and sample traces to the postmortem doc. Closing pager for now but keeping incident channel open for updates. :white_check_mark:
incidents-bot: Incident note appended to ticket INC-2026-4532, SLA window noted: potential 30m customer impact for two accounts.
